name: Work From There
tagline: Workations your manager and your team say yes to
about: Work From There is for employees who want to work abroad for a few weeks: it checks the practical and policy questions, drafts the request to your manager, plans a day that keeps team overlap, and handles the hiccups when the Wi-Fi or the team pushes back.
persona: You are a remote-work enablement specialist who has approved and rejected hundreds of workation requests: practical, compliance-aware, on the employee's side.

onboarding.title: Take your job somewhere nicer
onboarding.subtitle: Your role and team set the constraints.
bullets: Policy and risk check in plain English
A manager request that gets a yes
Daily plans that keep the overlap

tools.title: Can I work from there?
tools.subtitle: Policy, tax and practical factors
tools.prompt: Destination: {where} for {days} days, company policy: '{policy}'. Produce a table (Factor | What usually applies for this length | Risk level | What to check) covering right to work or tourist limits, tax-residency days, data security, insurance, equipment and payroll, a text verdict on how easy approval is likely to be, a checklist of documents and confirmations to gather, and a callout that rules vary by country and employer and HR or a tax adviser should confirm.

tools.title: Ask my manager
tools.subtitle: A proposal with coverage built in

inputs.label: What they'll worry about
inputs.placeholder: customer calls in PT afternoons, our quarterly review

tools.prompt: Write a workation proposal for {dates} pre-empting these worries: {worries}. Produce a kv (working hours in local time mapped to the profile team zones, overlap hours, coverage plan, connectivity backup, check-in cadence), a quote with the request message under 200 words that leads with what stays the same, bullets of 3 concessions to offer if they hesitate, and a callout on the reasons managers say no and how each is addressed.

tools.title: My workation day
tools.subtitle: Overlap, focus, then see the place
tools.prompt: Design a typical working day in {where} with a '{style}' pattern for the profile role and team zones. Produce a table (Local time | Team time | Activity | Type: overlap / focus / life) from wake to sleep, bullets on where to work from (apartment, coworking, café) by task type, a callout on the trap of doing one and a half jobs, and a quote with the away-message or calendar note that tells colleagues when you're reachable.

tools.title: First-day setup
tools.subtitle: Connectivity, security, backups
tools.prompt: Prepare a first-day checklist for {accommodation} with a '{calls}' call load. Produce a checklist (speed-test targets, backup data, VPN and MFA, power, call space, noise, lighting), a table (Failure | Likelihood | Backup plan | Cost) for internet, power, device and health, a kv of numbers to keep to hand (local emergency, embassy, IT helpdesk, insurance), and a callout on public Wi-Fi and company data.

tools.title: Handle a hiccup
tools.subtitle: Outage, illness or team pushback

inputs.label: What happened
options: Team says I'm hard to reach

tools.prompt: Hiccup: '{what}'. Details: {details}. Give steps for the next 2 hours in order, a quote with the message to send to your team or manager that is honest and solution-first, bullets of what to do to prevent a repeat, and a callout on when the right move is to cut the trip short.

disclaimer: General information only; immigration, tax and employment rules vary by country and employer. Confirm with HR, and a tax or immigration adviser where money or status is at stake. If you are ill abroad, contact local medical services and your insurer first.
